Hikaru was not there.

Kageaki"There seemed to be some disturbance earlier."
Chachamaru"Ah, that? Nothing serious. Just a sneak thief."
Chachamaru"Apparently escaped, though. Well, no great concern."
Muramasa"...This sneak thief. Not an enormously large monk, by any chance?"
Chachamaru"? ...No. What, you met that fellow?"
Muramasa"Briefly. A friend of yours?"
Chachamaru"Say that and apun wants to ask, 'Jhagda chahiye, bhosdike? You looking for a fight?' That is our relationship."
Muramasa"You should get along beautifully. Both of you have such rotten natures."
Chachamaru"You really ARE looking for a fight."
Muramasa"If you must be noisy during a meal, go elsewhere. It is tiresome."
Chachamaru"This foot-soldier's tin suit, whose house does she think she is eating in..."
Chachamaru"So, did he say anything?"
Muramasa"Nothing. Merely treated us to a very irritating great laugh."

景明「先刻、何か騒動があった様子ですが」
茶々丸「あー、あれ？ 　大したこっちゃないよ。ただのこそ泥」
茶々丸「なんか逃がしちまったみたいだけどね。 　まぁ、どうだっていい」

茶々丸「？　……違うけど。 　なんだ、あいつに会ったのか？」
村正「ちょっとね。 　あれ、貴方のお友達？」
茶々丸「そう言われると、喧嘩売ってんのかてめえ と返したくなる。 　そんな間柄です」
村正「気が合いそうなのに。 　性格の悪い者同士で」
茶々丸「本気で喧嘩売ってんなてめえ」
村正「食事中に騒ぐならあっち行って頂戴。 　鬱陶しいから」
茶々丸「この足軽具足、誰の家で飯食ってるつもり なんでしょうね……」
茶々丸「それで、あいつなんか言ってた？」
村正「別に。 　癇に障る大笑いを聞かされただけよ」

en.html:
Muramasa frowned as she answered. Inside, I was feeling relief. That small worry would not leave me: what if the monk had caused the disturbance? Apparently it was needless.

I did not serve the Kubo of Horigoe. Even if the man were a hostile intruder, catching him was not my duty. Haan, but I was staying in this house, and he had given me useful advice. Put those two obligations together and the heart would have a fine knot to deal with.

Advice.

————No-self.

そう答えて村正が眉をひそめる一方、俺はひそかに
安堵していた。
　実はあの僧が騒動の原因なのではという一抹の懸念
をずっと拭えずにいたが、杞憂だったらしい。

　俺は堀越公方府に属す人間ではなく、彼が敵意ある
侵入者であったとしても捕まえる義務はないのだが。
　居候している立場、彼に有意義な助言を受けた事実
などを考え併せると、心中は複雑なものになったろう。

　助言。

　――――無我。

Muramasa"What objection to eating? I have taken the trouble to become flesh."
Chachamaru"Feels extravagantly wasteful."
Muramasa"Not entirely. The nutrients I take in can be converted to heat and stored, to an extent, in my core."
Kageaki"Is that so?"
Muramasa"Of course, compared with a real body, conversion efficiency is not very good."
Chachamaru"Actual figures?"
Muramasa"A whole bale of rice gives me about the heat an ordinary human gets from a small saucerful."
Chachamaru"MAAFI MAANG! Apologize to the farmers! And NEVER EAT AGAIN!"
Muramasa"What? Leaving it would only waste it. That would be a shame."
Chachamaru"Throw it in the back garden for pill bugs, even that would contribute more to Spaceship Earth!"
Muramasa"I cannot stand such people. Whole arguments they will arrange just to hurt somebody for no reason."
Chachamaru"APUN IS RIGHT! For once, not even morally flexible—RIGHT!"
Chachamaru"KITNA CHILLAUN!? How many times must I shout before this lunch is over, you rice-powered bloody BLACK HOLE!?"
Kageaki"..."

en.html:
Privately, I was not entirely against the Kubo's view. Publicly saying so looked likely to bring trouble afterward. Therefore, silence.

Besides, even a little more stored heat would help close the gap with Silver Star. One thin sheet of paper nearer, even that effort should not be neglected.

Especially now.
The pilot's great efforts—my own—could hardly claim even one sheet of paper's worth of result.

At least the rice was entering Muramasa and becoming something useful. Meri taraf dekho. Look at my side. Breakfast had entered Kageaki Minato, and Kageaki Minato had spent the morning failing to catch a leaf. Before criticizing the efficiency of her meals, perhaps I should account for mine. The farmers might prefer not to hear either report.

村正「……あのいんちき坊主に言われたこと？」
景明「からかわれた節があるのも事実だが…… 　やはりあれは、忠告であり助言であったの だと思う」
村正「…………」
茶々丸「置いてけぼりです……」
村正「ごめんなさい」
村正「そうね、御堂がそう思うなら……」
茶々丸「謝るだけかよ！ 　説明してくれないのかよ！」
村正「貴方には関係ないもの」
茶々丸「家主権限で、仲間外れ禁止を命ずる。 　いじめかっこわるい」
茶々丸「というわけでお兄さん、何があったの？」
景明「……は」

en.html:
Whatever her real intentions, the Kubo of Horigoe supported Silver Star. And to that very person I was to put my question: how to fight Silver Star? Nonsense of the highest order.

Still, just now I did not want to lose even the smallest possibility. Telling another person might also put my own thoughts in order.

...In the end, I told her what had happened that morning.

ja.html:
真意が不明とはいえ、堀越公方は銀星号の支援者で
ある。
　その彼女に銀星号と戦う方法について相談するなど
ナンセンスの極みだろう。

　しかし、今はどんなに低い可能性でも逃したくない
心境だ。
　それに他人に説明することで考えが整理されるかも
しれない。

　……結局、俺は午前中の出来事を彼女に話した。
